faq.title: Frequently asked
faq.subtitle: Direct answers regarding our templates, customization process, and studio engineering.

items.question: Can you customize any Framer template?
items.answer: Yes. At The Spark Studio, we adapt and customize any official Framer marketplace template or third-party theme—adjusting brand palettes, typography, custom CMS fields, and third-party integrations.

items.question: What is the typical turnaround time?
items.answer: Template customizations are completed in 3 to 5 business days. Bespoke website builds take 2 to 3 weeks depending on scope.

items.question: How do you optimize Framer site speed?
items.answer: At The Spark Studio, we eliminate render-blocking fonts, compress assets to AVIF/WebP, and streamline responsive breakpoint trees to consistently achieve 95+ scores on Google PageSpeed Insights.

items.question: How do we get started?
items.answer: Email your project brief directly to The Spark Studio at hello@thesparkstudio.digital. We review your requirements and respond within 24 hours with a fixed quote and start date.

When marketing an eight-figure trophy estate, generic real estate websites fail. 

Most brokerage platforms are built on legacy MLS/IDX web templates engineered fifteen years ago. They clutter the screen with MLS registration popups, dense 50-field search boxes, low-resolution thumbnail grids, and bloated JavaScript suites that load in 4 to 6 seconds on mobile.

- **High-net-worth individuals (HNWIs) buy emotion, provenance, and privacy.** They browse properties like readers turn pages in *Architectural Digest* or examine rare art monographs, not like shoppers filtering commodity items on an e-commerce catalog.
- **Sluggish mobile speeds kill discretion.** Ultra-wealthy principals and their family office advisors browse on private mobile connections between flights and meetings. If an estate page stutters or takes three seconds to display photography, they leave.
- **Standard lead forms feel transactional.** Asking high-net-worth buyers for their personal telephone number before showing them floor plans feels intrusive. High-end conversions require bespoke VIP viewing intake desks and discrete representation options.

This is why top-producing brokers, boutique developer marketing teams, and luxury independent advisors are replacing legacy WordPress and IDX templates with **native Framer sites**. ## The 5 Pillars of High-Converting Luxury Real Estate Pages

A high-converting luxury real estate website requires distinct architectural choices. When customizing your chosen Framer template, verify that these five technical and design pillars are in place:

### 1. Cinematic Hero Immersion Under One Second
High-net-worth buyers evaluate luxury listings in less than three seconds. Avoid low-resolution photo sliders or slow-loading Vimeo embeds. Use compressed MP4/WebM video hero loops (under 4MB) hosted on a global CDN, accompanied by high-contrast typographic titles that immediately establish the architectural caliber of the property.

### 2. Curated Neighborhood & Lifestyle Storytelling
Buyers in prime markets are purchasing a lifestyle, not just square footage. Dedicate CMS pages or dedicated sub-sections to private airports, Michelin-starred dining, private schools, marinas, and private golf clubs. Havyn and Veyora demonstrate how lifestyle content builds local authority.

### 3. Dimensional Schematics & Materiality Ledgers
Discerning buyers want to inspect structural details: ceiling heights, imported stones, smart home automation, and floor plans. Templates like Onyx Atelier Pro include dedicated blueprint viewports and materials ledgers that validate eight-figure asking prices with technical clarity.

### 4. Discrete Pre-Qualifying Lead Intake Desk
Replace generic "Leave a Message" forms with a bespoke Private Viewing Desk. Include structured dropdowns for buyer representation (Principal, Family Office, Buyer's Broker) and confidential NDA requests. This pre-qualifies inquiries while providing buyers with privacy assurance.

### 5. Global Edge CDN Performance
Luxury buyers browse worldwide from London, New York, Dubai, Zurich, and Singapore. Framer deploys sites across a distributed edge CDN with automatic Brotli compression, image WebP conversion, and zero layout shift. Ensure your site maintains a sub-second First Contentful Paint (FCP) across all mobile devices.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions for Real Estate Brokers

### Can I connect an MLS / IDX feed to a Framer real estate template?
Yes. While Framer does not feature a native legacy IDX plugin like WordPress, modern brokerages connect their MLS data via Zapier, Make, or custom webhooks directly into the Framer CMS API. Alternatively, high-end brokers selectively curate their top 15–30 luxury listings manually in Framer CMS for editorial perfection, while linking search widgets to their regional MLS portal for commodity searches.

### How do I launch a custom single-property domain for a luxury listing?
Using templates like VALE House or Onyx Atelier, you can connect a custom vanity domain (e.g., *142oceanavenue.com*) in minutes:
1. Purchase the domain on Cloudflare, Namecheap, or Google Domains.
2. In Framer Site Settings, enter the custom domain.
3. Configure the two DNS A-records and one CNAME record provided by Framer.
4. Framer automatically provisions an SSL certificate within 5 minutes.

### How easy is it for non-technical marketing assistants to update listings?
Framer includes a dedicated Content Editor role. Assistants can log into the Framer CMS, add new property photos, update square footage, change asking prices, and publish changes in real time without touching the underlying design, layout, or code.

---

mobile-speed-framer-portfolio.title: How to find what slows down a Framer portfolio on mobile
mobile-speed-framer-portfolio.excerpt: Open one published project page on your phone. Watch the first screen.
mobile-speed-framer-portfolio.content:
Open one published project page on your phone. Watch the first screen. Does the title appear while the photograph is still empty? Or does the whole screen arrive late? Those two experiences feel equally slow, but they call for different fixes.

## How do you find the slow element on a Framer page?

Run the same URL through PageSpeed Insights in mobile mode. Find the element identified as Largest Contentful Paint (LCP). On an architecture portfolio it might be a photograph, but it can also be the project title. Record the element and timing over three runs before editing anything.

## What if the photograph appears late?

If the photograph is late, inspect the image actually downloaded at phone width. A full-resolution architectural elevation may be justified in a detail view, while the opening photograph only needs enough detail for the space it occupies. Try a smaller export. Compare both versions on a phone, paying attention to fine lines, shadows and lettering.

While you are on that page, open your browser’s developer tools, switch to the Network panel and reload at a phone-sized width. Sort by size. If the opening photograph is several megabytes, or is followed by a second large image that only appears further down, you have found where the first seconds go.

## What if the title appears late?

If the title is late, make a copy of the page and remove its entrance animation. Retest with the same font and layout. If the title appears sooner, you have narrowed the problem without touching the photography. Change one variable at a time and keep the version that makes the project readable sooner.

Fonts are the other common cause. If the title waits for a custom web font, every extra weight and style adds another download. Keep the weights you actually use, and check whether the same family is loaded twice under different names.

## What else slows a portfolio down on mobile?

Look at everything that is not part of the design itself: embedded maps, background videos, chat widgets, booking tools and tracking scripts. Each one runs on the phone’s processor while the page is starting. Remove one at a time on a copy of the page and measure again. If the page improves a lot, load that item later or replace it with a static image that links out.

## How do you know the fix worked?

Repeat the same three PageSpeed runs and compare the middle result, not the best one. Then open the live page on a real phone over mobile data. Field data from real visitors appears in the Core Web Vitals report in Google Search Console, which is based on the previous 28 days, so give a change about a month before judging it there.

furniture-product-page-photo-guide.title: What to put on a furniture product page before your next photo shoot
furniture-product-page-photo-guide.excerpt: A visitor considering a dining chair usually has three practical questions. Will it fit under the table?
furniture-product-page-photo-guide.content:
A visitor considering a dining chair usually has three practical questions. Will it fit under the table? What does the finish look like up close? How do I order the version in the photo? Build the page around those questions before choosing the final images.

## Which photos should a furniture product page show?

Start with one photograph that shows the whole chair. Follow it with a side view beside a table, then a close-up of the joint or upholstery. Give each photograph a job. A second front view in slightly different light is less useful than a clear measurement from floor to seat.

A simple shot list for most pieces: the whole piece at a three-quarter angle, a side view next to something familiar for scale, a close-up of the joint or material, the finish in natural light, and one photo of the piece in a real room. If the back or underside is visible in use, as with a sofa in the middle of a room, photograph that too.

## Where should dimensions and finishes go?

Put dimensions, units and the photographed finish close together. If the chair comes in oak and walnut, identify which one the visitor is looking at. When orders are made by enquiry, place the product name and finish beside that link so the buyer can ask about a specific piece.

Give height, width and depth, plus the measurements people check before buying: seat height for chairs, clearance under a table, the opening size of a cabinet. If you sell across countries, show both centimetres and inches. Lead time, delivery area and care instructions belong in the same block, not on a separate page.

## How should ordering or enquiries work?

If each piece is made to order, the enquiry button should sit next to the product name and selected finish, and the form should arrive already filled in with them. State the lead time near the button so the visitor knows what to expect before writing. A buyer who has to retype what they are looking at is a buyer who may not send the message.

## How do you test the layout before the photo shoot?
